title: Six weeks of emails: who we asked and what came back
summary: Six weeks, 462 emails and a lot of “not held”. Here’s who we wrote to, what they sent back, and what’s still waiting.
body: From 29 September to 9 November 2026 we swapped 462 emails with 49 organisations: 222 sent, 240 received. 87 of the replies were just automatic acknowledgements. 28 told us the information wasn’t held. 12 gave us part of what we asked, 9 carried disclosures and 8 refused. Every item is logged, with dates and sources, in the forensic journal.

HM Land Registry’s Wales Office replied on 4 November to our letter of 12 August. One straight answer: the “no question or doubt” statement sits in the 1982 application for first registration. It declined to alter the register or give indemnity, and pointed to the court. A separate request, F261029 and F261030, is due by 17 November.

South Wales Police finished internal review 1188/26 on 6 November and stuck with “no information held”. The first copy came on 26 October as a locked file with no password. FOI 1264/26 is still open, and the force has warned of a backlog past 20 working days. The Crown Prosecution Service replied on 21 October that it can’t take evidence from the public, and sent us back to the police.

Cadw answered ATISN 26-0009 on 6 November. The file on the 6 December 1988 decision not to list Great House Farm isn’t held. But Cadw sent five internal documents. An email of 1 June 2026 records that the file “has been destroyed”. A 2007 database extract lists file CL 72/381, dated 21 January 1993.

The Royal Commission wrote on 3 November that everything it holds is on Coflein site 20182, and three title records from 1926 and 1938 aren’t held. Heneb confirmed on 4 November, for the first time, that it searched both its digital and paper files. It doesn’t hold the 1983 to 1989 planning consultation letters.

Glamorgan Archives told us on 22 October that police occurrence books stop in 1984 and station logs in 1979. The 1988 Weekly Orders exist but are closed because they name serving officers. The National Library of Wales refused FOI/2026/16 on 4 November and pointed us to its reading room. The National Archives still hasn’t answered a request from 2 September.

Ordnance Survey has no record of who supplied the name, but sent five map extracts: “Ty-Mawr” in 1947, “Ty Mawr Farm” from between 1965 and 1971. Dŵr Cymru told us its 1980s records on the farm’s water supply are past retention and not held. Museum Wales holds nothing on the farm’s furniture and fittings.

The Ministry of Defence came back with nothing on 9 October. An email to the Cabinet Office on 31 October couldn’t be delivered. The ICO opened two cases, on 22 October and 3 November. And the Vale of Glamorgan Council’s scrutiny officer accepted our topic submission on 9 November. The earliest agenda it could reach, after the Chair’s screening, is 1 December 2026.

Still waiting, as of 10 November 2026: The National Archives (FOI CAS-361652 due 13 November, review CAS-356384 due 20 November, plus the overdue 2 September request). HM Land Registry, 17 November. DCMS and the Crown Prosecution Service, 18 November. The National Library of Wales, FOI2026/17, 25 November. Cadw ATISN 26-0141, the Ministry of Defence and the Wales Office, 26 November. South Wales Police FOI 1264/26, no date given. The council topic, 1 December. Two ICO cases, not decided yet. And two open questions: what record backs Cadw’s 1 June 2026 note, and whether the Royal Commission’s reply is a formal refusal with a right of review.
